_comment: Standing record of adversarial lead audits. gate.sh reads this so a green gate cannot coexist with an unsendable lead list. Update it only by running the audit again, never by hand.

audits.note: First audit. Six failure modes named: URL-prefix instead of operation; vendor-owned or generated SDK code; anchor on a declaration rather than a call; changed field absent from the repo; vendored dependency trees; line numbers from a different revision. All six gated.

Re-audit after gating all six. Same rate. The gates changed WHY leads die, not HOW OFTEN. Root cause named: verification proved co-location and never dependence. Ten of twenty leads were one cluster where the call sites matched correctly and the change still could not affect them, because removing a 204 while the 200 remains narrows the API rather than breaking it. Fixed at the findings level.

Third audit, after the verifier was rebuilt around a dependence proof (call reaching the operation by method and full path template; or a read of the changed field traced back to a vendor call). The proof chains were judged accurate in every case -- the paths, methods and operations were right. The leads are still wrong, for a reason the rebuild did not address: operation reachability was accepted as sufficient for a whole-schema removal, so a caller who reaches the operation but never reads the removed schema's fields is reported as affected. Seven of ten fell that way. This audit also found a FINDINGS defect no previous round had named, described below.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed.what: OpenAPI security is a list of ALTERNATIVES: [{A}, {B}] means A or B. Both the engine and the independent precision checker flattened it to a set of scheme names, so adding an alternative scored as breaking.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.evidence: Twilio DELETE /v2/Services/{Sid} went from [{accountSid_authToken}] to [{accountSid_authToken}, {access_token_bearer}]. Every existing caller kept working. Nine operations were scored breaking.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.why_it_survived: The checker shared the engine's mistake, so it agreed with it. That is precisely the failure a separate checker exists to prevent, and it means the earlier 86/86 claim was wrong for the security class.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.status: Fixed in both, independently. A change is breaking only when some old alternative can no longer be satisfied. Re-measured: 84 breaking findings, 84/84 confirmed, zero undecidable.

standing.blocker: Operation reachability is accepted as proof for a whole-schema removal. A caller who reaches the operation but never reads any field of the removed schema is not affected, and seven of ten audited leads were exactly that. The fix is to resolve the removed schema to its leaf field names in the OLD spec and require a read of one of them, rejecting calls whose response is discarded.
standing.findings_precision: 5-vendor gate population: 46/46 breaking, 68/68 potentially, zero undecidable. ALL 31 vendors with findings, 2026-08-21: 1332/1447 = 92.1% on independently decidable findings, 172 undecidable, over 1619 breaking findings. The full progression of every all-vendor number this project has ever claimed: 96.3% -> 67.8% -> 96.7% -> 77.8% -> 92.1%. Every drop is the checker learning to decide findings nobody had checked; none of the higher numbers was ever a measurement of the engine.
also_open: operation_reached() stops at the first affected operation with a hit, in list order, so an alphabetically earlier DELETE whose response is discarded wins over a GET whose response is deserialized. Rank by whether the response is consumed.

A lead's breaks_on names the finding's representative operation while its proof names the operation the file actually calls, with nothing stating the two are related. This misled three auditors who had the repo, the spec and the source in front of them.
standing.note: The findings engine is verified. The lead pipeline is not. Do not send outreach built on leads until an audit clears.
standing.blocker_fix_implemented: The prescribed schema_removed fix is in dependence.py: a proof requires a read of one of the deleted schema's own field names, and generic names cannot carry it. NOT YET AUDITED — lead_precision and sendable stay as they are until a fourth adversarial audit runs. Note the product direction has moved to `apidrift scan` against a consented checkout, where the cold-lead vantage problem does not arise.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.what: A schema is an implementation detail of an operation; a caller only ever sees the operation. Diffing schemas in isolation cannot tell a field being DELETED from a field being MOVED between two schemas that compose into the same operation, and the second breaks nobody.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.evidence: OpenAI removed `ResponseProperties.reasoning` in this window while `POST /responses` accepted `reasoning` throughout — it moved to another arm of the same allOf. Found by running the new `apidrift scan` against Azure-Samples/python-openai-demos, which reported reasoning.py:38 as broken. Five of 84 breaking findings were this class (OpenAI 3, Stripe 2).
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.why_it_survived: measure_precision.py asked the schema-level question — 'is the field still in this schema?' — which is the same question the engine asked, so it agreed. Identical shape to the security OR-of-AND defect above.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.status: Fixed in both, independently. The engine suppresses a removal when every affected operation still exposes the name; the checker now resolves each affected operation from the RAW document with its own resolver and refutes relocations on its own. Mutation-verified: with the engine's suppression disabled, the checker independently refutes exactly those 5 (23/28 = 82.1%).

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_3.what: A path parameter's NAME is OpenAPI-internal and never reaches the wire, exactly like a schema name. `/v2/Conversations/{Sid}` and `/v2/Conversations/{id}` produce byte-identical URLs for every concrete value, so renaming one moves no endpoint and breaks no caller. The same rename also surfaces as a param_removed plus a param_added_required, because a path parameter is positional in the URL rather than sent by name.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_3.evidence: Twilio renamed {Sid}->{id} and {ConversationSid}->{ConversationId} across Conversations and ControlPlane. That produced 15 of 79 breaking findings, plus 4 more param-level findings once renamed operations began being diffed body-to-body. Zero of the 19 break anybody.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_3.why_it_survived: dependence.paths_match() has ALWAYS normalised parameter names away when matching a caller's literal to a template — the engine knew names did not matter while PROVING and did not know it while DIFFING. measure_precision.py asked the spec author's question ('did the path string change?'), which is true for a rename. Third instance of a checker sharing the engine's assumption.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_3.status: Fixed in engine and checker independently. Also fixed a false NEGATIVE found alongside it: a renamed operation was never diffed body-to-body, so a vendor renaming a parameter and tightening the operation in one release had the second change go entirely unreported.

scan_standing._comment: The scan is a different vantage point from the leads and needs its own record. An Impact is a claim about a REPO; a finding is a claim about a SPEC diff. They are measured separately.
scan_standing.corpus: 22 public repositories that genuinely call these vendors, full checkouts, scanned at a 1095-day window. The previous corpus was the same repositories at 90 days, which is why it found nothing: the code was written years before the window opened.
scan_standing.note: All four initial impacts were refuted by hand against the source and the raw spec, and all four classes are now gated: a read proving a request-side change (phasehq/console), a keyword argument on the repo's OWN constructor counted as a request body (phasehq/console), and two of the same in autoevals/agentops. Zero impacts across 22 repos is a MEASUREMENT, not an absence — the Plaid fixture control still fires at the right line with exit 1.
known_blind_spots: API version pinning is now MODELLED for stripe/plaid/klaviyo/square, but only as an abstention. The tool cannot read which version an SDK release actually sends, so it reports UNMEASURED rather than diffing between the old SDK's version and the new one -- which is the diff a caller actually meets, on the day they upgrade.
The relocation suppressor consults a field map flattened at MAX_DEPTH=2 and abstains silently rather than marking the finding unchecked.
The spec cache is not fetched by default; a scan can run against a stale clone. `--fetch` is opt-in.
`_Assignments` is one flat module-level dict, so def-use tracing is scope-blind and flow-insensitive across function boundaries.
`--days` defaults to 90, which is the wrong default for the question. It has NOT been changed, because a longer default multiplies the population and the population is not yet audited clean.
Every language other than Python and JavaScript/TypeScript is counted and reported as UNMEASURED, never passed as clean.
scan_standing.pr_blocker: The fourth adversarial audit RAN on 2026-08-21 and found nothing to open a pull request about: 74 impacts sampled, 0 real. Five classes are now closed and the population must be re-audited before this flips -- a SMALLER population is not a MEASURED one. A fifth audit must sample the impacts that survive the fixes, and it must include the raw-HTTP callers specifically, because pinning removed every SDK caller of the biggest vendor from the judgeable population and nobody has yet checked what is left.

vendor_coverage.note: tools/vendor_check.py could not import until this session -- it was moved into tools/ and its sys.path and cache paths still pointed at the repo root, so every run died on line 12. The '20/22 working' number came from a copy that no longer exists.
vendor_coverage.unmeasured_reason: zero breaking findings in the window, so there is nothing to audit. Not a pass -- the report prints them as UNMEASURED rather than clean.
vendor_coverage.window_caveats: 14 of 21 carry one: an observed range shorter OR LONGER than requested (the old side is the last commit BEFORE the window, which for a quiet repo can be a year earlier -- openai 429d of 180d), or specs with no history behind them. sendgrid's HEAD is 2026-03-24, so its window ends five months before `asof`.

per_vendor_precision._note: zero breaking findings in the window, so nothing to audit. Printed as UNMEASURED, which is not a pass.

open_false_positive_classes._note: 115 findings the independent checker still refutes, 2026-08-21. 94 of them are ONE mechanism, named below and deliberately not fixed. That leaves 21 across six kinds.
open_false_positive_classes.the_one_mechanism: A response position that GAINS union arms. Twilio repointed a 200 body from `us_app_to_person` to a `oneOf` of it and a v2 superset; Cloudflare widened an Access policy `result` to `anyOf[app_policy, infra_policy]`; PayPal replaced `oneOf[error_400 ... error_500]` with one `error` object carrying every field. Every old key moves, so every field reads as removed, while a field present in EVERY new arm is still guaranteed. NO ENGINE FIX IS PROPOSED: the only rule that decides it is 'does every alternative still promise this field', which is verbatim the question the checker asks, and building it twice is how this project shipped the same defect six times. The checker catching them is worth more than the engine and the checker agreeing.

recall_controls._note: The gate had five layers and none asked whether the tool can still FIRE. Layers 1-5 all get quieter as the engine gets more conservative, so a suppressor that silenced everything would pass all five -- precision on zero findings is undefined, not zero. Layer 6 injects a break whose answer is known.
recall_controls.vendor_control: 235 controls fired across all 32 vendors, 0 MISSED, 0 found-but-refuted. Eight injections each.
recall_controls.scan_control: a fixture repo with the same dependence in Python AND TypeScript, built from findings re-derived on every run rather than read from a file. Both languages must fire.
recall_controls.corpus_scan: 9,240 files of real third-party code (Documenso, Formbricks, Langfuse, vercel/ai-chatbot), impacts held to a hand-verified baseline of 0. It reported 27 impacts before the co-location fix and 0 after, so it moves when scan precision moves.
caught: the checker refuting a real `GET /emails` removal because it keyed on PATH alone while an endpoint is METHOD+path
every vendor evidence marker being PYTHON-shaped, so `import { Resend } from 'resend'` matched nothing and TypeScript files were rejected at the prefilter and never examined
`_leaf_of` and `_named_identifier` disagreeing about what a finding names, so the scan prefilter demanded a SCHEMA name appear in source
a conflict resolution that kept a CONTROLS registry entry while dropping the function it names

scan_standing.window_note: 🚨 `--days 90` is the wrong default for the question `scan` asks. Integration code is written once and left; the caller's question is 'what has moved since we wrote this', not 'what moved this quarter'. 90 days: 0 impacts across 22 repos. 1095 days: 414. The zero was a window artefact and was read as precision for a whole day.

audits.what: Fourth adversarial audit, and the FIRST ever aimed at scan.py IMPACTS rather than leads -- the thing `pr_blocker` demanded.
audits.method: Stratified over every (kind, vendor) pair, max 3 per repo per stratum. Thirteen independent skeptics, ~6 impacts each, instructed to refute by default and to produce BOTH the production line whose behaviour changes and the raw-spec fact that makes it so. Every claim that survived went to two more refuters with different lenses (the code path, the spec document). Auditors read the raw documents through tools/spec_snapshot.py, which parses nothing and decides nothing.
audits.note: The findings engine measured 100% in the same run. An IMPACT is a claim about a REPO and a FINDING is a claim about a SPEC DIFF; nothing had ever measured the first one, and it was 0%.

scan_standing.impacts_found_note: 0 SURVIVING an adversarial audit -- not 0 emitted. The engine emitted 295 at a three-year window and the audit refuted every sampled one.

false_positive_classes_closed_2026_08_21.read_at_wrong_position: 21/74. A read matched on its LEAF WORD with nothing checking that it sat where the subject says. `subscription.currency` proved `<deleted_discount>.coupon.currency`. Closed by dependence.read_sits_where_subject_says (position) AND js_dependence._chain_reaches_change (reach) -- two questions, both needed: `subscription.discount.customer` passes reach and dies on position.
false_positive_classes_closed_2026_08_21.member_chain_without_provenance: ~13/74 across identifier_name_collision, local_function_not_vendor_call, local_method_call_not_api_operation, call_site_is_not_an_api_call, string_literal_matched_as_operation. `find_sdk_calls` accepted any chain whose spelling started with an idiom: a local list's `.append`, a dict's `.get`, the `secrets` stdlib module. Closed by requiring call_reaches_vendor on the chain's root, which is the gate JavaScript always had.
false_positive_classes_closed_2026_08_21.api_version_pinned: 3/74 sampled and structurally much larger. A dated-version vendor does not break a caller on an older version -- that is what the version is for. Closed by Vendor.versioned + ScanResult.pinned: SDK callers of stripe/plaid/klaviyo/square are UNMEASURED, raw-HTTP callers are still judged.
false_positive_classes_closed_2026_08_21.nullable_rewritten_as_anyof_null: OpenAPI 3.1 deleted `nullable`. Two OpenAI fields alone were 75 of the 295. Closed by loader._nullable_wrapper_payload in the schema view.
false_positive_classes_closed_2026_08_21.security_only_documented: 23 in the population. A document with no `securitySchemes` at all has no vocabulary for auth and its silence is undocumented, not unauthenticated. Closed by counting the old document's schemes and abstaining at zero.
false_positive_classes_closed_2026_08_21.cited_line_is_a_test_file: 8/74. Split into ScanResult.incidental and out of the exit status. Reported, never counted.

open_after_2026_08_21.request_field_type_widened: 6/74 and unfixed. `messages[]: object -> oneOf[...]`, `temperature: number -> anyOf[number, null]`. A request position that gains alternatives still accepts everything it accepted before. Same family as the response-side union-arm class already left open on purpose: the only rule that decides it is 'does every alternative still accept this', which is the question the CHECKER asks, and building it twice is how this project shipped the same defect six times.
open_after_2026_08_21.type_refactored_to_ref_same_shape: `CreateChatCompletionRequest.model: anyOf -> ->ModelIdsShared` where ModelIdsShared IS that anyOf. Extraction is notation. 32 in the population. The inlining direction is already closed (533babd); this is the same rule with the arrow reversed.

population_after_the_fixes.note: A SMALLER population is not a MEASURED one. These 65 have NOT been audited; the 74-impact sample that produced 0/66 was drawn from the 295 that stood after position and reach, and every class closed since removes members of it.

what_dominates_what_is_left.openai_request_widening: 22 of 65. `CreateChatCompletionRequest.model: anyOf -> ->ModelIdsShared` and `messages[]: object -> oneOf`. A request position that gains alternatives still accepts everything it accepted before, and `model`'s union carries a bare `{type: string}` arm on BOTH sides, so nothing was ever narrowed.
what_dominates_what_is_left.github_response_union_widening: 22 of 65. `integration.owner` and `commit.author` went from `anyOf: [null, simple-user]` to `oneOf: [simple-user, enterprise]` / `[simple-user, empty-object]`. Checked against the raw document rather than assumed: these are NOT notation, a reader really can now receive an arm it did not expect. The class stays open and stays the CHECKER's question.
what_dominates_what_is_left.pinned: 281 files across the corpus reach a dated-version vendor through its SDK and are reported UNMEASURED rather than judged. That is a large share of the code that used to produce impacts.

scan_standing.performance: posthog, the largest repo in the corpus, takes 16m39s at a 1095-day window. That is not a CI gate anybody keeps. Unfixed and unmeasured beyond this one number.

independent_cross_check.why: Layers 1-6 are all apidrift checking apidrift, including the recall controls, whose stimulus this repo's author chooses. An independent implementation can surface a break nobody here thought of.

recall_holes.mechanism: flattened as Field(type='__truncated__') past MAX_DEPTH=2; the truncation abstention then silences it
recall_holes.verified: by hand against the raw old/new spec3.json

recall_holes.missed: 200 body repointed from $ref terminal.reader to an anyOf, dropping required device_type
recall_holes.mechanism: apidrift sees device_type on neither side
recall_holes.verified: by hand against the raw old/new spec3.json

independent_cross_check.corrects_the_record: The `truncated` abstention is recorded as MEASURED UNSAFE because narrowing it deleted 49 confirmed findings. That measured its PRECISION cost. Its RECALL cost had never been measured by anything, and hole 1 is it. Both numbers are now on the table; neither alone decides the rule.
independent_cross_check.open_severity_split: apidrift calls request-property removal potentially_breaking; oasdiff calls it breaking. Stripe rejects unknown params, so a caller that sends the removed property does break. Unresolved.
independent_cross_check.oracle_not_authority: 577,044 to apidrift's 4 on the same pair. 367,596 were response-property-enum-value-added and 209,438 were response-optional-property-removed -- the fan-out collapse() exists to prevent. Only the disagreements carry information.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_5.what: A schema NAME never reaches the wire. `schema_removed` was 1007 of the 2766 breaking findings across all 21 vendors -- 36% of the population -- and the precision checker confirmed 1007 of 1007.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_5.evidence: The checker's test was `name in schemas_of(old) and name not in schemas_of(new)`, the same question the engine asks and the SPEC AUTHOR's question. Asked the caller's way -- find every $ref to it in the OLD document and look at the same place in the NEW one -- 694 of the 1007 are refuted. Klaviyo inlined 208 single-value enums at the identical property; Cloudflare renamed 191 response envelopes in bulk; PayPal's error_409 lived only inside error_default, one restructure reported 92 times; Sentry's whole components table is vestigial because it publishes a DEREFERENCED spec.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_5.why_it_survived: Fifth instance of the checker sharing the engine's question, and the largest by an order of magnitude. All-vendor precision was never 96.3%; it was 67.8%.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_5.status: Fixed in engine and checker independently, four suppression classes (unreachable / relocated / renamed / subsumed), each decided by a different question. Every one has a mutation in BOTH directions.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_6.what: A refuter whose precondition holds for 100% of inputs is a broken instrument, not a result.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_6.evidence: The first version of the `unreachable` rule refuted any schema with no $ref pointing at it. Sentry's openapi-derefed.json contains ZERO occurrences of `"$ref"` in 3.2 MB, so the test was vacuously true for all 157 of its schemas. An adversarial audit showed it would have deleted a real break: DetailedOrganizationSerializerWithProjectsAndTeams is verbatim the 200 body of a PUT that still exists and lost seven required response properties.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_6.why_it_survived: It did not -- it was killed before shipping, by an audit run specifically to attack the new rules. Recorded because the shape recurs: this is the same failure as 'zero results is a failed measurement until a control says otherwise', applied to a suppressor instead of a search.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_6.status: Both engine and checker now count the document's linking constructs first and ABSTAIN when there are none, in their own separate states (`unreachable_unmeasurable` / UNDECIDABLE). Measured: Sentry is the only fully-dereferenced vendor in the corpus; every other carries 502-17,807 refs.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_7.what: `newly required` is a claim about BODIES, and both engine and checker asked about a `required:` ARRAY. The caller's question is whether a JSON body the OLD document accepted is REJECTED by the NEW one. Two shapes satisfy the array test and fail that one: the enclosing OBJECT is itself new, so no body the old document accepted could contain it and the obligation is additive; and the obligation was already there while only the flattener's KEY moved.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_7.evidence: Whole class re-adjudicated from the raw documents, all 158 findings, no sampling: 47 TRUE / 109 FALSE / 2 undecidable. Cloudflare `PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/devices/policy` gained an OPTIONAL `global_acceleration` object with four required members -- the body's own obligation set is empty before and after, so nothing that validated stopped validating; 4 findings. Cloudflare bulk-renamed all 13 arms of `access_schemas-identity-providers` to `access_identity-providers-2` and added a 14th; every arm required `config`, `name` and `type` before and after; 42 findings. Cloudflare `POST /accounts/{account_id}/workers/workers/{worker_id}/versions` gained `exports_reconciliation` with 9 required members, all optional to send -- and the ONE real break in that operation, `urls` becoming mandatory, was already reported separately as `schema_field_added_required`.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_7.why_it_survived: Sixth instance of the checker sharing the engine's question, and the first where sharing it produced errors in BOTH directions. 103 of 158 came back UNDECIDABLE because `collapse()` rewrites the path to `<Schema>.a.b` and the checker walked the schema NAME as a property -- undecidable for a purely notational reason, which is not a measurement of anything. 12 more were falsely REFUTED because the checker read one node's `required` array and never merged `allOf`: Sentry's `statusDetails` is an `allOf` arm requiring seven names where the old object required none, and it read as `required new=False`.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_7.status: Fixed in engine and checker independently. Engine (`apidrift/diff.py`): two suppressors on the BARE path -- `_subtree_is_new` (an ancestor absent from the old flattening) and an obligation every old route already carried -- each abstaining when the old side flattened to nothing, which is the doctrine-3b control. Checker (`tests/measure_precision.py`): `required_everywhere` builds the obligation set a validator would enforce (allOf UNIONS, oneOf/anyOf INTERSECT) and `descend` asks whether an old-valid body could reach the node at all; a per-arm obligation the union does not carry is UNDECIDABLE, not refuted, because deciding it needs an old-arm/new-arm correspondence the documents do not state.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_7.measured: 5-vendor gate population 49 -> 47 findings, 47/47 = 100%; the two dropped were hand-verified false against the raw specs (stripe `POST /v1/financial_connections/sessions` `limits.accounts` and twilio `POST /v2/ControlPlane/Configurations` `conversationsV1Bridge.serviceId` -- both bodies require exactly the same names before and after). All 21 vendors: 1874 -> 1767 findings, 1492/1537 = 97.1% -> 1498/1531 = 97.8%, refuted 45 -> 33, undecidable 337 -> 236. This class: 25/33 with 103 undecidable -> 29/29 with 0 undecidable (added_required) and 16/20 with 2 undecidable -> 18/18 with 4 undecidable (now_required).
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_7.doctrine_3_verified_at_scale: With the engine's two suppressors disabled the engine emits 1874 findings and the independent checker refutes 140 UNAIDED, 107 of them this class (29/136 = 21.3%). With them on the engine emits 1767 and the checker refutes 33, none of them this class. The suppressed set and the independently-refuted set are the same 107.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_7.recall_control: 120 controls fired, 0 MISSED, 0 found-but-refuted, across 22/22 vendors -- up from 99 because a NEW injection was added. `inject_request_field_added_required` lands at the TOP of a body, where neither suppressor's precondition can hold, so it could not have detected either rule over-firing. `inject_nested_request_field_added_required` puts the requirement on an object that ALREADY EXISTED in the old body, which is the exact shape `_subtree_is_new` must not swallow.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_7.mutations: 11 new, both directions for every rule, 156/156 killed. Three of them SURVIVED on the first run because the union-arm tests were decorative: written as a bare inline `anyOf`, the arm marker lands in ROOT position and `_strip_root_marker` erases it, so the existing `_blind` rule already matched the two sides and the field never reached the code under test. Rewritten around a `$ref` to a NAMED union of NAMED arms, which is Cloudflare's real shape and leaves the arm marker interior.
